mcqs.question: Which of the following equations represents a displacement reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal (Zn) displaces a less reactive metal (Cu) from its compound. Option A shows this. Option B is a double displacement (precipitation) reaction, C is a combination, and D is a combustion reaction.

mcqs.question: Why can zinc displace copper from copper(II) sulfate solution?

options.A: Zinc is more reactive than copper.
options.B: Zinc has a higher atomic mass than copper.
options.C: Copper is more reactive than zinc.
options.D: The reaction occurs only at high temperature.

mcqs.answer: Zinc is more reactive than copper.
mcqs.explanation: The reactivity series shows zinc above copper, meaning zinc has a greater tendency to lose electrons and therefore can displace copper from its salt. Atomic mass does not determine reactivity, and temperature is not the controlling factor here.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: How can the reactivity series be used to predict the products of a metal reacting with a solution of another metal's salt?

options.A: A metal higher in the series will displace the metal lower in the series from its salt.
options.B: A metal lower in the series will displace the metal higher in the series from its salt.
options.C: Metals react only if they are adjacent in the reactivity series.
options.D: The reactivity series predicts only the colour of the precipitate formed.

mcqs.answer: A metal higher in the series will displace the metal lower in the series from its salt.
mcqs.explanation: The reactivity series ranks metals by their tendency to lose electrons. A metal placed higher (more reactive) can replace a less reactive metal from its compound. Options B, C, and D misinterpret the series.

mcqs.question: Which of the following equations best illustrates a double displacement (metathesis) reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In a double displacement reaction, the cations and anions exchange partners, forming new compounds. Option A shows this exchange. Option B is a single displacement, C is a combination, and D is a decomposition reaction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions will produce a solid precipitate?
mcqs.explanation: Barium sulfate (BaSO4) is insoluble in water, so it precipitates as a solid. The other reactions involve soluble salts or gas evolution, not precipitate formation.

mcqs.question: A student places an iron nail into a copper(II) sulfate solution. Which observation confirms that a displacement reaction has occurred?

options.A: The solution turns blue, iron dissolves, and copper metal deposits on the nail.
options.B: The solution becomes colourless and no solid forms.
options.C: The temperature of the solution rises sharply.
options.D: Bubbles of gas are evolved from the solution.

mcqs.answer: The solution turns blue, iron dissolves, and copper metal deposits on the nail.
mcqs.explanation: Iron, being more reactive than copper, displaces copper ions, forming iron(II) sulfate (blue solution) and depositing copper metal. The colour change and metal deposition are characteristic of a displacement reaction. The other options describe different types of reactions.

mcqs.question: Statement: "If a metal does not react with water, it cannot displace any metal from its salt solution." Is this statement correct?

options.B: False, because reactivity with water is not the only factor determining displacement ability.
options.C: True, but only for alkali metals.
options.D: False, but only for transition metals.

mcqs.answer: False, because reactivity with water is not the only factor determining displacement ability.
mcqs.explanation: A metal may be unreactive with water yet still be able to displace a less reactive metal from its salt (e.g., zinc does not react vigorously with cold water but displaces copper from CuSO4). Hence the statement is a misconception.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: Given the reactivity series Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Cu, what will happen when a piece of aluminium metal is placed in an aqueous solution of iron(II) sulfate?

options.A: Iron metal will be displaced and deposit on the aluminium surface.
options.B: Aluminium will be displaced and go into solution.
options.C: No reaction will occur because both metals are below magnesium.
options.D: Magnesium will be displaced from the solution.

mcqs.answer: Iron metal will be displaced and deposit on the aluminium surface.
mcqs.explanation: Aluminium is higher (more reactive) than iron in the series, so it can displace iron ions from FeSO4, forming aluminium sulfate and depositing iron metal. Options B and D describe impossible scenarios, and C ignores the relative positions of Al and Fe.
